chunks: What the Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me of, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥafṣ ibn al-Bakhtarī, who said:
A woman came to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام and asked him about a woman whose bleeding continues, and she does not know whether it is hayd or something else.

He said, so he said to her: «Indeed, the blood of hayd is hot, fresh, black; it has force and heat. And the blood of istihadah is yellow and cold. So when the blood has heat, force, and blackness, then she should leave the salat (prayer).»
He said: Then she left while saying: If he had been a woman, he would not have added anything beyond this.

key_terms.أَسْوَدُ: black, a sign indicating hayd in this context
key_terms.الدَّمُ: blood, the subject being examined for legal classification
key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ: salat (prayer), which is to be left when the bleeding is judged to be hayd
key_terms.الِاسْتِحَاضَةِ: non-menstrual irregular bleeding with different legal rulings
key_terms.الْحَيْضِ: menstrual bleeding that carries specific legal rulings
key_terms.بَارِدٌ: cold, a distinguishing characteristic of istihadah blood here
key_terms.حَارٌّ: hot, a distinguishing characteristic of hayd blood in this report
key_terms.دَفْعٌ: forceful flow or pressure, described as a sign of hayd blood

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام distinguish between hayd and istihadah in ongoing bleeding?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal criterion for distinguishing hayd from istihadah based on the observable qualities of the blood. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام describes the signs of each and links that distinction to the ruling of leaving the salat (prayer) during hayd.
